lesson_title: 22/7 Is Not Pi: The Real Number System
hook_text: Your teacher told you pi is 22 over 7. It isn't — and the difference is the whole topic.
clip_script: A common confusion must be cleared at once. The fraction 22 over 7 is NOT pi. It is a rational approximation: 22 divided by 7 is 3,142857 142857... — recurring, hence rational — and it agrees with pi only to two decimal places. Pi itself is 3,14159265... and no block ever repeats. That is the whole test: a decimal that stops or repeats is rational; a decimal that never stops and never repeats is irrational. Now the square root of 9 — is it irrational? It equals 3. A natural number. Always simplify the root before you classify it.
visual_style: Two digit-streams race across the screen: 22/7 falls into a looping 142857 block that glows green and repeats, while pi's digits scatter in random colours and never loop; a root sign over 9 snaps shut into a bold 3.
pacing: Slow on the 22/7 reveal, quick on the repeat-or-not test, punchy on the root 9 twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and classify every number on the list yourself.
